battle.name: 黃天蕩之戰
battle.theater: 長江南岸鎮江黃天蕩江段
battle.brief: 建炎四年正月，金兀朮率追擊大軍至瓜洲、揚州江面，欲再渡長江直搗建康。韓世忠自楚州馳抵鎮江，以舟師分扼黃天蕩上下游，斷金人歸路，相持四十有八日，糧援俱絕。配重投石車一類攻城器械在江面無用，金人只得以飛翼船強攻而不成。終值大風夜，兀朮斫纜濟江遁走，韓世忠追至建康不及。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 交戰的兩方是金國與南宋。金方由金太原王完顏宗弼，漢名兀朮，率領追擊大軍，他以行元帥、都元帥之號統諸軍，麾下有萬戶都統與漢軍將佐。建炎四年正月初，兀朮自通州、燕京一線南下，率精騎追宋高宗至瓜洲、揚州江面，又用海船組成舟師，載人載馬載糧，順揚子江溯江西上，與粘罕即完顏宗翰率到的援軍會合，攻楚州不克，才沿江東指建康。金國的指揮系統以金主完顏亶的軍令為樞，兀朮臨機處置，粘罕與兀朮在淮上會師後分掌騎兵與舟師，漢軍降將亦隨軍聽用。宋方是南宋朝廷，高宗趙構在建炎三年冬自揚州退保杭州，其時樞密院與中書分掌軍政，張浚、趙鼎一系主戰，秦檜主和，議論未決。江南沿江的實際指揮落在江淮馬步軍都統韓世忠手上，他自海州率部兼程而下楚州，舟師駐鎮江江口；張俊、劉光世兩軍屯於建康兩岸與江北要地，奉詔策應而逗留不進；另遣舟師分扼黃天蕩上下游，以斷金軍退路。戰役由韓世忠一人主持水面封鎖，中樞無力他顧。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Jin state and the Southern Song. On the Jin side the field command belonged to the Prince of Jin, Wanyan Zongbi, better known by his Chinese name Wuzhu, who led the pursuing army with the titles of commander of the march and commander-in-chief of all the armies; under him stood the commanders of the ten-thousand households together with Chinese defectors in the ranks. In the first month of the fourth year of Jianyan he marched south from the Tongzhou and Yanjing line with his picked cavalry, pursued the Song emperor down to the waters of Guazhou and Yangzhou, and then built a fleet of sea-going ships that carried men, horses and grain upstream along the Yangzi, to join the reinforcements brought by Jihan, that is Wanyan Zonghan, who had come south in his own right; failing at Chuizhou they turned down the river towards Jiankang. The Jin chain of command ran from the war orders of the ruler Wanyan Dan, while Wuzhu settled what had to be settled on the spot; after Jihan joined him above the Huai the cavalry and the flotilla were divided between the two commanders, and surrendered Chinese officers served in the same ranks. On the Song side was the Southern Song court, with Gaozong Zhao Gou, who had fallen back from Yangzhou to Hangzhou in the winter of the third year of Jianyan; the Privy Council and the Secretariat divided military and civil authority, Zhang Jun and Zhao Ding pressing for war while Qin Hui argued for peace and the question was still undecided. The real command on the river lay with Han Shizhong, commander of the cavalry and infantry of the Jiang and Huai, who brought his men down by forced march from Haizhou to Chuizhou and anchored his flotilla at the mouth of the river off Zhenjiang; the armies of Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi lay about Jiankang on both banks and at the strong points north of the river, ordered to support him and never came; other detachments of river troops were posted above and below Huangtiandang to cut the Jin road back. The blockade of the water was accordingly directed by Han Shizhong alone, the central court having nothing to spare for anything else.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩方。宋方領軍者是韓世忠，字良臣，綏州綏德人，出軍籍，宣和末從西夏與金人轉戰，靖康之變率數百騎追金人至汴京，一軍之中以「鐵骨」稱之。建炎四年正月，他自海州率師兼程而下，泊舟鎮江，以水軍獨當一面，戰至百餘合，屢挫金舟；金人乞和、賄以金帛求借道，他一律不許。宋高宗及朝廷重臣自瓜洲脫身後，數次要沿江諸郡交出韓世忠以贖高宗，他都拒絕，謂當與金人決戰於江上。他的妻子張氏亦隨軍督戰，傳記稱其親執桴鼓以勵士卒，但正史未詳其事，姑存其說。金方主帥是完顏宗弼，即兀朮，金太祖庶長子，自幼隨軍，宣和末領兵追宋人南渡，建炎三年冬曾一度追高宗至瓜洲渡而不得手。他狡黠而能忍，重騎射而輕舟事，屢破宋軍於淮上，直抵黃天蕩才遇上以水軍專長的對手。另一名金將粘罕即完顏宗翰，建炎四年率兵南下與兀朮會合，攻楚州不克，其後兵權被收，兀朮乃獨握大軍。朝廷層面，高宗趙構在行在收到警報即倉皇西遷，輾轉浙東、江西、閩北，紹興元年二月才還杭州；樞密使趙鼎與張浚力主整軍北伐，對金的追擊只能靠水軍硬擋；宰相秦檜則力主議和，戰後以朝廷自有計議為由收兵權、罷韓世忠樞密使之職，使這場血戰的功臣在次年即被調離中樞。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belong to the two sides alike. On the Song side the man in command was Han Shizhong, courtesy name Liangchen, of Suide in Suizhou, born into a military family, who had campaigned against the Western Xia and the Jin in the last years of Xuanhe, and who at the time of the Jingkang disaster led several hundred horsemen in pursuit of the Jin as far as Bianjing, so that his men spoke of him in the army as a man of iron bones. In the first month of the fourth year of Jianyan he brought his troops down by forced march from Haizhou, anchored his ships at Zhenjiang, and with a river force single-handedly took the burden of the defence, fighting a hundred and more engagements and repeatedly striking the Jin flotilla; when the Jin begged for peace and offered treasure and silk in the hope of buying a passage, he refused them all. After Gaozong and the ministers of the court had escaped from Guazhou, they several times asked the districts along the river to hand Han Shizhong over in exchange for the emperor, and each time he declined, saying that the matter must be settled by a fight on the river with the Jin. His wife, née Zhang, went with the army in the camp and there is a tradition that she beat the war drum in person to steady the soldiers, though the official histories do not set out the matter in detail, so it is best kept as a tradition. On the Jin side the commander-in-chief was Wanyan Zongbi, that is Wuzhu, a younger son of the founder of the Jin, who had been in the army from childhood and had led troops in pursuit of the Song southward in the last years of Xuanhe, and who in the winter of the third year of Jianyan had once pursued Gaozong as far as the crossing of Guazhou without catching him. He was cunning and patient, strong in the saddle and awkward on the water, and he had broken Song armies repeatedly above the Huai; only at Huangtiandang did he meet an opponent whose strength lay in ships. The other Jin commander was Jihan, that is Wanyan Zonghan, who came south in the fourth year of Jianyan and joined Wuzhu, failed to take Chuizhou, and was afterwards stripped of his command, leaving Wuzhu to hold the whole army. At the level of the court, Gaozong Zhao Gou, on receiving the alarm in his temporary capital, fled west in haste and wandered through eastern Zhejiang, Jiangxi and northern Fujian, not returning to Hangzhou until the second month of the first year of Shaoxing; the Privy Councillor Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun pressed for a reorganisation of the army and a northern expedition, so that the only answer to the Jin pursuit had to be a river force; the Chancellor Qin Hui pressed hard for negotiation, and after the battle he used the argument that the court had its own arrangements to draw in the troops' command and to remove Han Shizhong from the office of Privy Councillor, so that the hero of the bloody stand was shifted out of the central command as early as the following year.
kits: 這場戰爭的裝備主軸是舟船，不是攻城器械。配重投石車在卡面上標為一一〇〇年的義大利形制，說的是十二世紀初的歐洲：義大利城邦在十一世紀末至十二世紀初已用配重式投石車對付城牆與塔樓，其機械原理與中國一系的拋石機同源，唐宋砲車一路發展至《武經總要》所載的長臂配重圖式，即屬此類；金人南下時亦攜帶砲車與雲梯、飛梯、撞車、攻城塔，用於攻宋城池，屬攻方工程。但黃天蕩是江面遭遇戰，投石車這類靠長臂拋射石彈的兵器只能架在岸上，發石沉重、落點散、難以命中在急流中梭織的舟船，故正史對此役使用投石車並無記載；金人在江上真正投入的攻城技術是飛翼船，把城樓高台架到船上企圖高壓宋軍，韓世忠的應手是鉤槳與鐵鉤纏鬥，鉤住船身使之隨水而退，逼得飛翼船不能進逼。金軍舟師以海船數百艘為主，兼載人馬糧械；宋軍則以梢船，即密舵散篷、遇風即泊、遇敵則划櫓的小艇，配海鰍快船貼身近射，輔以強弓硬弩、標槍、火箭與霹靂炮一類火器，並把漁船改作載兵與載燃油的火船。糧秣方面，金軍自淮北運糧，渡江之後接應全靠北岸，困守四十有八日之後糧盡，遂以金帛買路；宋軍糧食由建康、池州沿江輸送，各軍寨存糧不過數日。
kitsEn: The backbone of the equipment in this war was the boat, not the siege engine. The counterweight trebuchet on the card is given as an Italian form of the year 1100, which refers to early twelfth-century Europe: the Italian city-states were already using the counterweight trebuchet against walls and towers from the end of the eleventh and the beginning of the twelfth century, and its mechanical principle is the same as that of the Chinese line of stone-throwing engines, the cannon carts of the Tang and Song running on to the long counterweighted arm recorded in the diagrams of the Wujing Zongyao; the Jin brought cannon carts, ladders, flying ladders, battering rams and siege towers south with them for use against Song cities, and these belonged to the engineering of the attacker. But Huangtiandang was a meeting engagement on the water. A weapon like the trebuchet, which throws a stone on the end of a long arm, could only be set up on the bank; its shot was heavy, its fall scattered, and it could hardly hit ships weaving through a racing current, so the official histories record no use of trebuchets in this action. The siege technology the Jin actually put on the river was the flying-wing ship, a tower-like superstructure built onto a hull so as to command the Song boats from above; Han Shizhong answered it with hook-poles and iron grapnels, catching the hull so that the current carried it back and the flying-wing ship could never close. The Jin flotilla rested mainly on several hundred sea-going ships carrying men, horses and stores as well. On the Song side the force was built from shao-chuan, small boats with a concealed steering oar and a folding screen that could be struck down at once in a wind and worked with oars in an engagement, together with hai-qiu fast boats that closed in to shoot at close range, supported by strong bows and crossbows, javelins, fire arrows and fire weapons of the thunder-crash family, while fishing boats were converted into troop boats and into fire boats carrying oil. Supply was decisive in the same way: the Jin drew their grain from north of the Huai, and once across the river all replenishment depended on the far bank, so that after forty-eight days of confinement their food ran out and they tried to buy a road with treasure and silk; the Song brought their provisions by water from Jiankang and Chizhou, and the stores in the river garrisons lasted only a few days.
tactics: 金軍的戰術是騎兵突進配合舟師溯江，目的是在宋廷崩潰之際一舉擒住高宗。兀朮不與宋軍糾纏於城下，而以精騎疾馳兩岸、迫降沿江鎮寨，把舟師留在身後順流直上；渡江處以海船連綴、繩索相繫成浮梁，一次過河，這是建炎三年冬瓜洲渡的成法，四年正月再東來時仍欲照辦。遭韓世忠封江之後，金人一度以飛翼船強行靠岸射擊，又屢遣偏師登岸掠取糧秣與船隻，皆被宋軍擊退；糧盡之後連遣使議和、賂以金帛求借道，韓世忠不許。金軍的戰術由此由攻轉困，坐待風汛。宋軍的戰術可以概括為封江斷渡四字。韓世忠不急於求戰，而以舟師分置黃天蕩上下游，扼其來路與退路，使金舟夾在江心不能上下；主力以梢船往來穿梭，近距離射擊金軍船舷，迫其無法靠岸接援；岸上則設營壘與砲位，抵禦金兵登岸反攻。金兵糧盡求和之日，兀朮終以夜半大風遣舟師斫纜乘流而下，盡潰而走，韓世忠追至建康而不及。整場戰役的勝負關鍵，不在兩軍的兵力，而在江面那條補給線的長短：金軍的補給線斷在江心，宋軍的補給線斷在江岸之外。
tacticsEn: The Jin tactic was a cavalry thrust supported by a flotilla moving up the river, the object being to seize Gaozong in the moment when the Song court was coming apart. Wuzhu did not wish to be drawn into a siege under the Song cities; instead he drove his picked cavalry along both banks, reducing the river towns as he came, and kept the boats behind him to run up the stream. Where he meant to cross he lashed sea-going ships together with ropes into a floating causeway and put the army over in one body, which was the method that had carried him across at the Guazhou crossing in the winter of the third year of Jianyan, and which he meant to repeat when he came east again in the first month of the fourth year. Once Han Shizhong had sealed the river, the Jin tried once more to work the flying-wing ships in close and shoot from them, and sent detached parties ashore repeatedly to seize grain and boats, and in every case were driven back by the Song; when their food was gone they sent envoys to treat and offered treasure and silk for a passage, and Han Shizhong refused. Their method therefore changed from attack to endurance, waiting on the wind and the season. The Song method can be summed up in four words: seal the river and cut the crossing. Han Shizhong did not press for a decision; he posted river troops above and below Huangtiandang to hold the road in and the road out, so that the Jin ships sat in mid-river unable to go up or down; his main force worked in and out among the enemy in light craft, shooting the Jin hulls at close range and preventing them from coming alongside to take on stores; on the bank he raised camps and battery positions to hold off the counter-attacks of the Jin who tried to land. On the day the Jin sued for peace, Wuzhu finally took advantage of a great wind in the middle of the night and sent his boatmen to cut the cables and drift down with the current, and the whole force broke away, while Han Shizhong pursued them as far as Jiankang without catching them. The decisive factor in the whole engagement was not the relative strength of the two armies but the length of the supply line on the water: the Jin supply line was cut in mid-river, while the Song supply line was cut off short of the bank.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰役起於建炎四年正月，時值公元一一三〇年初春；金兀朮自通州南下、追宋高宗至瓜洲，是建炎三年冬的行動，本年正月再率大軍續至揚州、六合一線，與粘罕援軍會合後沿江東指。韓世忠所部水軍兵數各家記載不一，大致在數千至萬餘之間；金軍追擊之眾，宋人記為數萬，有誇稱十萬者，實際當以數萬為近。相持日數，通行記載為四十有八日，一說在六十日上下。金軍舟船數百艘，多為海船改裝，兼載人馬；韓軍以梢船、快船配合，數亦以百計。金人自瓜洲至建康一線的江道約三百餘里，兀朮脫圍後韓世忠追之不及，本役乃終。前一年十二月金人追高宗至瓜洲渡，距行在一日之程；本年正月高宗自杭州西遷，輾轉撫州、福州，紹興元年二月方還杭州。戰後宋廷於建炎四年五月起反覆商議和議，紹興元年十一月宋金訂約，宋向金稱臣、歲貢銀絹各二十五萬，割和尚原等陝西之地。此役之後韓世忠於紹興元年被罷樞密使，張俊與劉光世同罷兵權，韓世忠僅留鎮江軍節度使鎮守楚州。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The action began in the first month of the fourth year of Jianyan, which corresponds to the early spring of the year 1130. Wuzhu's march south from Tongzhou and his pursuit of Gaozong to Guazhou belonged to the winter of the third year of Jianyan; in the first month of the fourth year he brought the main army on again to the Yangzhou and Liuhe line, joined the reinforcements of Jihan, and then turned down the river. The strength of Han Shizhong's river force is given differently by different writers, roughly from a few thousand to somewhat over ten thousand; the pursuing Jin host is recorded by the Song as a several tens of thousands, with some claiming a hundred thousand, and the nearer figure is the one to be preferred. The number of days of stalemate is commonly given as forty-eight, with one account putting it at about sixty. The Jin had several hundred vessels, mostly converted sea-going ships carrying men and horses as well; the Song matched them with light craft and fast boats, again by the hundred. The river run from Guazhou to Jiankang is about three hundred li, and the pursuit ended when Wuzhu got away. In the twelfth month of the year before, the Jin reached the Guazhou crossing with the emperor only a day's journey from his temporary capital; in the first month of this year Gaozong moved west from Hangzhou, wandering through Fuzhou and Changle, and did not return to Hangzhou until the second month of the first year of Shaoxing. After the battle the court debated terms from the fifth month of the fourth year of Jianyan, and in the eleventh month of the first year of Shaoxing the Song and the Jin concluded a treaty by which the Song called itself a subject, paid silver and silk to the value of two hundred and fifty thousand each year, and ceded places such as Heshangyuan in Shaanxi. In the wake of this action Han Shizhong was removed from the office of Privy Councillor in the first year of Shaoxing, Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi were likewise stripped of their commands, and Han Shizhong was left only as military governor of Zhenjiang to hold Chuizhou.
cause: 起因是金軍對宋高宗的追殺與南宋江防的倉促應對。建炎三年冬，金人渡江追高宗至瓜洲，行在僅隔數十里，江南人心震動；宋廷倉促間只能沿江布防，而在淮上用兵者，張俊、劉光世各擁重兵而思自保，韓世忠一人獨負江防。建炎四年正月，金主完顏亶命兀朮再度南下，目標是一舉渡江直抵建康，終結南宋；粘罕率兵來會，兩軍在淮上合流，先攻楚州不克，遂順江而下。對宋方而言，瓜洲距行在太近，此時已無退路可守，唯有一戰。金人看準的正是宋廷的分裂：主戰派欲乘勝北伐而兵力分散，主和派只想割地換安寧，江防因此時薄時厚，鎮江、瓜洲一線的守兵既無城可依又無援可恃，韓世忠得以獨斷獨行還有一個原因，是他的水軍經驗與金人騎兵恰好相剋：金人擅長野戰奔衝而拙於舟楫，宋軍正好以船技術補上這個缺口。
causeEn: The cause was the Jin pursuit of the Song emperor and the hasty way the Southern Song river defence was improvised. In the winter of the third year of Jianyan the Jin crossed the river in pursuit of Gaozong as far as Guazhou, the temporary capital was a mere ten li away, and the people of Jiangnan were shaken; the court could only spread its troops along the river in haste, and of the commanders in the Huai country Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi each held a heavy force while thinking first of their own safety, so that Han Shizhong bore the whole burden of the river defence alone. In the first month of the fourth year of Jianyan the Jin ruler Wanyan Dan ordered Wuzhu south once more, with the object of crossing the river and striking straight at Jiankang to end the Southern Song; Jihan came south to join him, the two armies merged above the Huai, they failed at Chuizhou first, and then went down the river. On the Song side the nearness of Guazhou to the imperial camp left no ground to fall back upon, and there was nothing to be done but to fight. What the Jin counted on was the division in the Song court: the war party wanted to march north in pursuit of victory and had its strength scattered, the peace party wanted only land for quiet, and the river defence was therefore thick at one moment and thin at another, so that the garrisons on the Zhenjiang and Guazhou line had neither a city to stand in nor succour to expect. There was a second reason why Han Shizhong was left to act on his own: the experience of his river force matched the Jin cavalry exactly in reverse. The Jin were at their best in the open field and clumsy with oars and hulls, and the Song had just the craft to fill that gap.
impact: 這場戰爭第一次讓金國明白，追擊高宗的騎兵大軍在長江水面會被一支小船隊鎖住。韓世忠封江四十有八日，金人既不能渡，也不能退，雖然終於藉大風脫身，卻丟掉了渡江追亡的全部時間差，宋高宗得以輾轉脫身，紹興元年二月還杭州，南宋朝廷在江南站穩了腳跟，南宋國祚由此再延一百五十年，直到一二七九年亡於蒙古。對宋人而言，這是靖康之變以後第一次成建制的軍事勝利，士氣為之一振，也為其後順昌、郾城兩場大捷提供了信心與兵源。對朝廷而言，勝利卻沒有帶來勝利：秦檜以和議為名收兵權，張俊、劉光世被罷，韓世忠被罷樞密使、鎮守楚州，紹興元年十一月的和約幾乎把黃天蕩換成了歲幣與稱臣，抗金一系在主和派手中出局。技術上，此役確立了南宋守江而非守城的國策，也說明十二世紀攻城器械的進步不等於戰爭的進步：配重投石車在歐洲正改寫攻城攻防，在黃天蕩卻全無用武之地，能鎖住騎兵的是船，不是砲。
impactEn: This war taught the Jin state for the first time that a cavalry army in pursuit of an emperor could be locked in place on the Yangzi by a handful of small boats. Han Shizhong sealed the river for forty-eight days; the Jin could neither cross nor retire, and although they finally got away on a great wind they lost the whole margin of time that the crossing depended on, while Gaozong escaped and was back in Hangzhou in the second month of the first year of Shaoxing. The Southern Song court planted its feet in Jiangnan, and the state lived another hundred and fifty years, not falling to the Mongols until 1279. To the Song this was the first organised military victory since the Jingkang disaster, it lifted the spirit of the troops, and it supplied the confidence and the manpower for the later victories at Shunchang and Yancheng. At the level of the court, however, the victory brought no victory: Qin Hui used the negotiations as a cover for drawing in the troops' command, Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi were dismissed, Han Shizhong was removed from the office of Privy Councillor and sent to hold Chuizhou, and the treaty of the eleventh month of the first year of Shaoxing very nearly exchanged Huangtiandang for a yearly tribute and a formula of submission, and the war party left the court in the hands of the peace party. In technical terms the action established the Southern Song policy of holding the river rather than the cities, and it showed that progress in siege machinery in the twelfth century is not the same thing as progress in war: while the counterweight trebuchet was rewriting the attack and defence of castles in Europe, it was of no use whatever at Huangtiandang. What held the cavalry was the boat, not the stone-thrower.
result: 結果是一場沒有全勝的封阻戰。金軍被困黃天蕩四十有八日，糧盡援絕，兀朮先遣使議和、賄以金帛求借道，韓世忠不許；終值大風之夜，金人遣舟師斫纜乘流而下，盡數夜遁，韓世忠引兵追至建康而不及。韓軍沒有擒到兀朮，也沒有攻佔任何城池，但金軍本來的目的，即渡江直取行在，已經完全落空。此後金人再沒有組織起同等規模的追擊兵力，南宋在江南獲得喘息之機，宋廷得以把黃天蕩的軍功兌換成紹興和議：建炎四年五月起罷張俊、劉光世兵權，紹興元年罷韓世忠樞密使之職，同年十一月與金訂約。從裝備的結果看，這場戰役給出的答案是清楚的：十二世紀最好的攻城器械在江面上毫無意義，能封住金國最精銳的追擊大軍的，是梢船、海鰍快船、火箭與一條被切斷的江面補給線；金人帶來的砲車與攻城塔始終沒有機會上架。
resultEn: The outcome was a blockade that ended without a complete victory. The Jin were held in Huangtiandang for forty-eight days with food exhausted and no relief; Wuzhu first sent envoys to treat, and then offered treasure and silk for a passage, and Han Shizhong refused him; in the end, on a night of great wind, the Jin boatmen cut their cables and ran down with the current and the whole force escaped in the dark, while Han Shizhong pursued them to Jiankang and did not come up with them. The Song army took neither Wuzhu nor a single city, but the Jin purpose, a crossing to strike straight at the imperial camp, had failed outright. After this the Jin never again assembled a pursuing force of the same size, the Southern Song gained room to breathe in Jiangnan, and the court was able to convert the achievement at Huangtiandang into the settlement of the first year of Shaoxing: from the fifth month of the fourth year of Jianyan the commands of Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi were drawn in, in the first year of Shaoxing Han Shizhong was removed from the office of Privy Councillor, and in the eleventh month of the same year the treaty was concluded with the Jin. As to the equipment, this engagement gives a clear answer: the best siege machinery of the twelfth century was meaningless on the water, and what held the finest pursuing army the Jin had was the shao-chuan boat, the hai-qiu fast boat, the fire arrow and a river supply line that had been cut. The cannon carts and siege towers the Jin brought with them never got the chance to be set up.
